name: JARVIS-1
institution: Team CraftJarvis — Peking University (PKU), Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT), UCLA, BIGAI (Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence)
what_evolved: Context记忆与提示 — a growing multimodal memory that stores successfully-executed plans/skills (goals, plans, milestone items) and is retrieved as in-context demonstrations to augment planning. No model weight updates; evolution is purely in-context/memory-based.
skill_as_artifact: Yes. Skills exist as reusable memory entries in a multimodal key-value store: keys = (task text + visual observation/situation), values = the natural-language action plan that was successfully executed. These persisted trajectories are independently retrievable and reusable artifacts.
skill_encoding: Natural-language plans (ordered crafting/mining/smelting sub-goal sequences) paired with multimodal state keys (task text + visual observation). Text keys embedded via CLIP text encoder; visual states via CLIP visual encoder. Memory file is assets/memory.json.
skill_granularity: Sub-task workflow — each skill is a decomposed chain of intermediate sub-goals / milestone items (e.g. obtain_wooden_pickaxe -> mine_cobblestone -> craft_furnace -> smelt_iron -> ...). The MLM also performs backward sub-goal decomposition for retrieval.
how_method: imitation_demonstration (self-imitation) — only successful trajectories are saved and later retrieved as retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) in-context demonstrations. Augmented by a curriculum-driven self-instruct exploration loop. No gradient updates, no RL.
learning_signal_source: 成败轨迹 (success/failure trajectories) — task success gates whether a plan is written to memory; failures are discarded, successes are stored and re-used.
reward_granularity: outcome — binary task completion (target item obtained within time budget) determines memory storage.
learning_paradigm: online (live Minecraft interaction); on-policy (agent's own experiences); in-context (memory-as-context, no gradient). Distributed speculative execution across shared memory accelerates data collection.
when_evolve: Both inter-test-time (multi-epoch self-improving loop: agent traverses the whole task-pool for N epochs, accumulating experiences into shared memory) and intra-test-time (within a long-horizon episode the success rate on milestone items keeps rising as game time extends and as memory grows).
trigger: curriculum驱动 (LLM-self-instructed task curriculum that follows the Minecraft tech tree) across epochs; plus failure-triggered interactive re-planning (self-check/self-explain) within an episode when a sub-goal fails.
library_structure: Multimodal key-value memory (flat store indexed by task + observation). Entries organized by task/sub-goal with multimodal embeddings; optionally shared/centralized across distributed environments. Hierarchical retrieval via backward sub-goal reasoning.
retrieval_method: 语义相似度 (semantic similarity) via CLIP — text-embedding similarity between query and task key to filter candidates, then visual-state embedding similarity to rank; combined with generation-as-retrieval (LLM backward reasoning produces sub-goal textual queries; current visual observation is appended to form a multimodal query). Top entry per sub-goal retrieved as RAG demonstration.
validation: execution-based validation gating — a plan is only persisted to memory after it has been successfully executed in the environment (target item obtained). Failed executions are not stored.
error_correction: 自我修订 (self-revision) — MLM self-check spots missing/incorrect items in the initial plan and self-explain repairs it; on execution failure the agent re-perceives state (e.g. broken pickaxe, missing fuel) and dynamically re-plans from current inventory.
test_env: Minecraft (Minecraft Universe Benchmark / MCU; native human-like observation & action space at 20 FPS, mouse+keyboard).
backbone_model: Multimodal LM = MineCLIP (vision-language foundation model) chained with an LLM. LLM options tested: GPT-4, ChatGPT, LLaMA2-70B, and a Minecraft-finetuned LLaMA2-13B (≈ChatGPT). Low-level goal-conditioned controller = STEVE-1 (built on VPT).
where_deploy: general (open-world generalist multi-task agent); demonstrated in Minecraft.
metrics: success_rate (% episodes over >=30 seeds), long-horizon milestone completion, skill_library_growth (number of successful trajectories / memory size), cross-task transfer (success-rate gain from retrieved experiences), ablation across LLM backbones and curricula.
key_results: (1) Completes >200 MCU tasks with near-perfect performance on short-horizon tasks. (2) ObtainDiamondPickaxe: 12.5% success at 60 min (6.22% at 20 min) vs 2.5%/3% for RL-finetuned VPT (SOTA) — a ~5x reliability gain. (3) Self-improving: over 4 epochs it accumulates 425 successful trajectories and success rate on intermediate milestone items keeps rising. (4) GPT-generated curriculum beats human-written and random curricula. (5) Minecraft-finetuned LLaMA2-13B matches ChatGPT; stock LLaMA2-70B underperforms due to lack of Minecraft knowledge.
limitations: transferability (Minecraft/MCU-specific, no cross-game transfer shown); controller execution fidelity is the bottleneck for diamond-tier tasks (STEVE-1 cannot perfectly execute the LLM's short-horizon instructions); LLM planning hallucinations; situation-aware planning errors cause inefficiency/failure; open-sourced code omits multimodal descriptor, multimodal retrieval, and online learning modules (only offline fixed-memory eval released).
